mainTopic: Can owners or a כהן who are טמא have offerings brought and accepted? The גמרא tests זקני דרום using the פסח laws and the ציץ.
overview: This amud keeps testing the view of זקני דרום, that someone who is טמא מת may still have his offerings brought. First the גמרא says the requirement 'איש לפי אכלו' (being able to eat the פסח) is only the ideal way (למצוה). A ברייתא seems to link eaters to the registered (מנויין), but זקני דרום do not accept that linkage. The גמרא then challenges them with a קל וחומר from טומאת שרץ to טומאת מת. Next it brings a משנה: the ציץ helps for impure blood but not for טומאת הגוף, which seems to mean owners who are טמא מת cannot send offerings. The answer is that the משנה is about a כהן who is טמא שרץ. That reading survives a challenge from רבי חייא about טומאת התהום (he only excludes זיבה) and a challenge from רמי בר חמא's question (he disagrees with זקני דרום). The amud ends by opening a new proof from the פסוק about the ציץ, and that proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The eating requirement is only an ideal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting the challenge 'לפי אכלו' and answers that it is only a לכתחילה מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The earlier challenge was:] 'according to his eating!' Answer: That is only for the מצוה (the ideal way), not a requirement that disqualifies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes an earlier challenge based on the פסוק 'איש לפי אכלו.' It answers that the need to be able to eat the פסח is only the ideal way to do it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge said someone who cannot eat the פסח (like a טמא מת) should not have it brought for him at all. The answer limits the פסוק to לכתחילה. If it was done anyway, the offering is not ruined.

keyTerms.meaning: 'According to his eating': the פסח is counted for those who can eat it
For the ideal fulfillment of the מצוה, not a requirement that disqualifies

phrases.english: "according to his eating!"
phrases.notes: This finishes a question from just before: שמות 12:4, 'איש לפי אכלו.'

phrases.english: It is for the מצוה (ideally).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a challenge raised just before this section began.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'לפי אכלו' disqualifies a פסח brought for someone who cannot eat.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'לפי אכלו' is only the ideal; after the fact the offering is valid.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows registration is required even after the fact
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that slaughtering for people who are not registered disqualifies the פסח. Since eaters are linked to the registered in the פסוק, eating should also be required.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is it not required even after the fact? But a ברייתא teaches: 'במכסת נפשות' teaches that the פסח is slaughtered only for those registered for it. If he slaughtered it for people who are not registered, you might think he just failed to do the מצוה properly. So the פסוק says 'תכסו.' The פסוק repeated it to make it a requirement that disqualifies. And the eaters are compared to the registered!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer 'למצוה.' It cites a ברייתא showing that registration (מנויין) is a requirement that disqualifies the offering, and eating is linked to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק places 'במכסת נפשות' (registration) right next to 'איש לפי אכלו' (eating). This placement creates a היקש, a comparison between the two. The repeated word 'תכסו' shows registration is required even after the fact. Because of the היקש, being able to eat should be required after the fact too.

keyTerms.meaning: To be required even after the fact (without it the offering is invalid)
Those registered for the פסח
'By the count of souls' (שמות 12:4)
The פסוק repeated it, which shows it is required even after the fact
Compared through a היקש, because the two appear side by side in the פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up 'מצוה' and 'עיכוב.' A מצוה is the right way to do something. An עיכוב means that without it the offering does not work at all.

phrases.english: And it is not required after the fact?!
But it was taught: "By the count of souls"
teaches that the פסח is not slaughtered
except for those registered for it.
If he slaughtered it not for its registered people,
one might think it is just like failing to do the מצוה properly?
So the verse says: "You shall count"
phrases.notes: Same פסוק, שמות 12:4. The idea of counting shows up a second time.

phrases.english: The verse repeated it to make it required after the fact.
And the eaters are compared to the registered!

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'לפי אכלו' is only לכתחילה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Registration is required after the fact, and a היקש links eaters to the registered, so eating is required after the fact too.

steps.title: זקני דרום do not use the comparison
steps.stepSummary: זקני דרום do not accept the היקש between eaters and the registered.
steps.simpleTranslation: זקני דרום do not compare them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that זקני דרום simply do not make the comparison between eaters and the registered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer accepts the ברייתא about registration. It only rejects the step that carries that rule over to eating. For זקני דרום, eating stays a לכתחילה matter.

keyTerms.meaning: The Elders of the South, whose view is being examined
They do not make the היקש (comparison)

phrases.english: The Elders of the South do not make the comparison.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Eaters are compared to the registered, so eating is required after the fact.
steps.terutzMaskana: זקני דרום do not make that comparison.

steps.title: A קל וחומר from שרץ to מת
steps.stepSummary: Even without the היקש, a קל וחומר shows a כהן who is טמא מת should not be able to make an offering acceptable.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even if they do not compare, they still have a refutation from this. Look at owners who became impure from a שרץ: they may send their offerings even ideally, and still a כהן impure from a שרץ cannot make an offering acceptable. Now look at owners who became impure from a dead body: they may not send their offerings ideally. Then a כהן impure from a dead body, isn't it logical that he cannot make an offering acceptable?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks זקני דרום from a new direction, using a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טומאת מת is more severe for owners than טומאת שרץ, because a טמא מת owner should not send his offering לכתחילה. A כהן with the lighter טומאת שרץ already cannot be מרצה. So a כהן with the more severe טומאת מת certainly should not be מרצה. This goes against זקני דרום.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation
The owners of the offering
A creeping animal whose carcass causes a lighter טומאה
Makes the offering acceptable for the owner
Send their offerings to be brought for them

phrases.english: And even if they do not compare,
from this too they have a refutation:
Just as where the owners became impure from a שרץ,
where they may send their offerings even ideally,
a כהן who became impure from a שרץ cannot make it acceptable;
where the owners became impure from a dead body,
where they may not send their offerings ideally,
a כהן who became impure from a dead body,
is it not logical that he cannot make it acceptable?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי לָא מַקְּשִׁי נָמֵי מֵהָא נָמֵי אִית לְהוּ פִּירְכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts that זקני דרום reject the היקש, but attacks them with logic instead.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of זקני דרום that a כהן who is טמא מת can be מרצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר: the owners' rules show טומאת מת is more severe than טומאת שרץ, so a כהן who is טמא מת should certainly not be מרצה.

steps.title: The ציץ does not help for bodily impurity
steps.stepSummary: An objection from a משנה: for a נזיר and one bringing a פסח, the ציץ helps for טומאת דם but not for טומאת הגוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: because they said that for a נזיר and one who brings a פסח, the ציץ makes acceptable for impurity of the blood, but the ציץ does not make acceptable for impurity of the body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another objection (מיתיבי) against זקני דרום from a ruling about the ציץ. It is quoting the source here and will analyze it next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ציץ can fix the problem when the blood of the offering became impure. It does not fix the problem of a person's body being impure. The next step works out whose impurity this is and shows why it seems to go against זקני דרום, who hold that owners who are טמא מת may still send their offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: The כהן גדול's golden frontplate, which can make up for certain impurity
Impurity of a person's body
Impurity of the offering's blood

phrases.english: They objected: because they said:
phrases.notes: This is from a משנה in פסחים 80b.

phrases.english: a נזיר and one who brings a פסח,
the ציץ makes acceptable for impurity of the blood,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין הַצִּיץ מְרַצֶּה עַל טוּמְאַת הַגּוּף.
phrases.english: but the ציץ does not make acceptable for impurity of the body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge against זקני דרום, this time from a תנאי source.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ציץ does not cover טומאת הגוף. Step 6 shows this must mean טומאת מת of the owners, so owners who are טמא מת could not have their offerings brought, against זקני דרום.

steps.title: Which impurity does the משנה mean? It must be מת, which contradicts זקני דרום
steps.stepSummary: The טומאת הגוף in the משנה cannot be שרץ, since we slaughter a פסח for one who is טמא שרץ. So it must be טומאת מת, and that shows the owners cannot send their offerings, against זקני דרום.
steps.simpleTranslation: What kind of impurity is the משנה talking about? If you say a שרץ, you already said we slaughter and sprinkle for someone who is טמא from a שרץ! So it must mean impurity from a dead body. And the משנה teaches that the ציץ does not help. This shows that if the owners became טמא מת, they cannot send their offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is completing the challenge it started in step 5. It shows that the משנה must be talking about טומאת מת, and that this goes against זקני דרום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are only two choices for the impurity in the משנה. It cannot be שרץ, because we already know a פסח may be brought for someone who is טמא שרץ. That leaves מת, and the משנה says the ציץ does not help for it. That means a טמא מת owner cannot have his offering brought, which is the opposite of what we said in the name of זקני דרום.

keyTerms.meaning: A dead creeping creature that makes a person טמא for one day
Impurity from a dead human body, which lasts seven days
Makes the offering acceptable
The owners of the offering
They send their offerings to be brought for them

phrases.english: With what [kind of impurity is the משנה dealing]?
phrases.notes: This goes back to the משנה from step 5, which says the ציץ does not help for טומאת הגוף.

phrases.english: If you say with impurity of a שרץ,
but you said: We slaughter and sprinkle
for one who has impurity of a שרץ!
phrases.notes: He means the פסח. Someone who is טמא שרץ will be טהור by nighttime, in time to eat it.

phrases.english: Rather, [it means] impurity of a dead body;
and it teaches: The ציץ does not make it acceptable;
this shows that if the owners became טמא from a dead body,
they do not send their offerings!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge from the משנה that began in step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of זקני דרום that owners who are טמא מת may send their offerings
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The impurity in the משנה must be מת, because שרץ is ruled out. The משנה says the ציץ does not help for it, so owners who are טמא מת cannot have their offerings brought.

steps.title: The משנה is about a כהן who is טמא from a שרץ
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that owners who are טמא מת may send their offerings. It explains that the משנה is not about the owners at all but about a כהן who became טמא from a שרץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. If the owners became טמא from a dead body, that is indeed so. Here we are dealing with a case where the כהן became טמא from a שרץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by moving the משנה to a different case. The impurity in the משנה belongs to the כהן doing the service, not to the owners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed the משנה was talking about the owners' impurity. The answer says the משנה is talking about the כהן's impurity, which is a different situation. So the rule of זקני דרום about owners who are טמא מת stays in place, and the משנה teaches that the ציץ does not help when the כהן himself is טמא שרץ.

keyTerms.meaning: That is indeed so; yes, we agree
What case are we dealing with here? (used to narrow a source to a specific case)
The כהן who performs the service

phrases.english: No; if the owners became טמא from a dead body,
that is indeed so;
phrases.notes: He means: yes, in that case the owners may still send their offerings, just as זקני דרום said.

phrases.english: here, what are we dealing with?
A case where the כהן became טמא from a שרץ.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא; אִי דְּאִיטַּמּוֹ בְּעָלִים בְּמֵת – הָכִי נָמֵי
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the case of the משנה (הכא במאי עסקינן)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's טומאת הגוף refers to the owners, so it must mean טומאת מת
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה refers to a כהן who is טמא שרץ. Owners who are טמא מת may still send their offerings.

steps.title: The סיפא about טומאת התהום cannot be about a שרץ
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא says the ציץ helps for טומאת התהום. But רבי חייא teaches that טומאת התהום applies only to מת, which seems to exclude שרץ. So the משנה cannot be about a שרץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, say the last part of the משנה: If he became טמא with טומאת התהום, the ציץ makes it acceptable. But רבי חייא taught: They said טומאת התהום only for a dead body. 'Only for a dead body' comes to exclude what? Doesn't it come to exclude טומאת התהום of a שרץ?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 7 using the last part of the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה is about a כהן who is טמא שרץ, then the סיפא, which says the ציץ helps for טומאת התהום, must also be about a שרץ. But רבי חייא says the special rule of טומאת התהום applies only to מת. That seems to mean it does not apply to שרץ, so the משנה would not be talking about שרץ.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of the משנה
Impurity from a hidden source that nobody knew about, literally 'impurity of the depths'
To exclude

steps.confusionAlert: טומאת התהום does not simply mean any impurity underground. It means an impurity whose source was hidden and unknown to everyone at the time, like a buried body no one knew about, and was only discovered afterward.

phrases.english: If so, say the last part [of the משנה]:
If he became טמא with impurity of the depths, the ציץ makes it acceptable.
But רבי חייא taught:
They did not say [the rule of] impurity of the depths
except for a dead body alone;
'For a dead body' comes to exclude what?
Doesn't it come to exclude impurity of the depths from a שרץ?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 7 from the סיפא of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה is about a כהן who is טמא שרץ
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא applies טומאת התהום to the case of the משנה. רבי חייא limits טומאת התהום to מת, which seems to exclude שרץ, so the משנה cannot be about שרץ.

steps.title: רבי חייא only excludes זיבה
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא's word 'only for מת' comes to exclude טומאת התהום of זיבה, not of שרץ. So the משנה can still be about a כהן who is טמא שרץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It comes to exclude טומאת התהום of זיבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining that רבי חייא is excluding a different kind of impurity, זיבה. With this, the explanation from step 7 holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that 'only for מת' was meant to rule out שרץ. The answer says it rules out only זיבה. So hidden שרץ impurity can still be included with מת in the rule of טומאת התהום, and the משנה can be talking about a כהן who is טמא שרץ.

keyTerms.meaning: The impurity of a זב, from a discharge of the body

steps.whatToRemember: According to זקני דרום, owners who are טמא מת may still send their offerings. The משנה that says the ציץ does not help is about a כהן who is טמא שרץ. רבי חייא's rule that טומאת התהום applies only to מת excludes זיבה, not שרץ.

phrases.english: No; it comes to exclude impurity of the depths from זיבה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8 and keeps the explanation of step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading what רבי חייא's limiting word excludes
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Only for מת' excludes only זיבה, so שרץ may be included and the משנה can be about a כהן who is טמא שרץ.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא's question should already be answered
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה is about a טמא כהן, then רמי בר חמא's question about a כהן with טומאת התהום is already solved by the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about the question of רמי בר חמא: a כהן who brings the offerings of a נזיר and a פסח, is טומאת התהום allowed for him or not? Solve it from our משנה, which says the ציץ helps for טומאת התהום, since we are now saying the משנה is about a כהן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 7, that the משנה is about a כהן who is טמא. If so, a well-known open question of רמי בר חמא should already be answered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רמי בר חמא asked whether a כהן who did not know he was טמא (טומאת התהום) can still bring a נזיר's or a פסח's offering. Our משנה's סיפא says the ציץ helps for טומאת התהום. If the משנה is about a כהן, the answer is 'yes', so why did רמי בר חמא need to ask?

keyTerms.meaning: The one who makes the offering accepted, meaning the כהן doing the עבודה
Hidden טומאה that no one knew about, like a buried dead body
Solve it, settle the question
We are dealing with this case

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶלָּא הָא דְּבָעֵי רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא:
phrases.english: But this question that רמי בר חמא asked:
a כהן who brings their offerings to be accepted
phrases.notes: 'Their' means the נזיר and the person bringing a פסח from our משנה.

phrases.english: was טומאת התהום permitted for him,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ לֹא הוּתְּרָה לוֹ טוּמְאַת הַתְּהוֹם?
phrases.english: or was טומאת התהום not permitted for him?
Solve it: טומאת התהום was permitted for him,
since here we are dealing with a כהן!
phrases.notes: 'Here' is our משנה, which Step 7 explained as being about a כהן.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא הָא דְּבָעֵי רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 9 kept the 'כהן טמא שרץ' reading alive, the גמרא raises a new problem with that reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation of זקני דרום that the משנה is about a כהן (Step 7).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the משנה is about a כהן, its סיפא directly answers רמי בר חמא's question, so his question would make no sense.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא disagrees with this reading
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא surely disagrees with זקני דרום and does not read the משנה as being about a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רמי בר חמא simply does not hold like זקני דרום. He reads the משנה differently, so for him the question stays open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge only works if everyone agrees the משנה is about a כהן. רמי בר חמא reads the משנה as being about the owners, so the משנה tells him nothing about the כהן. The reading of זקני דרום still stands for those who follow it.

keyTerms.meaning: Certainly
They disagree

phrases.english: As for רמי בר חמא, they certainly disagree.
phrases.notes: He means רמי בר חמא and זקני דרום disagree about what the משנה is talking about.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Disagreement: the source of the question does not hold the challenged opinion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone reads the משנה as being about a כהן, so רמי בר חמא's question is already answered.
steps.terutzMaskana: רמי בר חמא reads the משנה differently from זקני דרום, so his question is still open, and זקני דרום's reading is not disproven.
steps.whatToRemember: זקני דרום read the משנה as being about a כהן who is טמא שרץ. רמי בר חמא does not, so he can still ask about טומאת התהום for a כהן.

steps.title: A new proof from the verse about the frontplate
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a new source: the פסוק says אהרן bears the sin of the holy things, and asks which sin that is.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'And Aaron shall bear the sin of the holy things.' Which sin does he bear?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new proof with 'תא שמע', quoting the פסוק about the ציץ. This line only sets things up; the answer to 'which sin' comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the ציץ lets אהרן 'carry' a sin connected to קדשים. The question 'which sin?' will lead to which kind of problem the ציץ fixes. That will be used to test the issues discussed above.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall bear (carry)
The sin of the holy things
The gold frontplate worn by the כהן גדול

phrases.english: Come and hear:
'And Aaron shall bear the sin of the holy things'
phrases.notes: שמות 28:38, the פסוק about the ציץ.

phrases.english: Now which sin does he bear?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: וְנָשָׂא אַהֲרֹן אֶת עֲוֹן הַקֳּדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the רמי בר חמא challenge is settled, the גמרא turns to a new source.
steps.raayaObject: Which kind of sin or problem the ציץ makes up for.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק in שמות 28:38 and its explanation, which continues on the next amud.
